🎙 Legal diplomacy must deliver tangible results in protecting national interests: Iran official

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs Kazem Gharibabadi has called for a results-oriented approach to legal and multilateral diplomacy, stressing that international engagement must produce tangible outcomes in defending Iran’s national interests and securing the rights of its people.

Gharibabadi made the remarks at a meeting of legal and international affairs directors and experts at the Foreign Ministry in Tehran on Thursday, where he reviewed the ministry’s activities over the past 18 months, including during the two wars of aggression imposed by the United States and Israel.
​
He said diplomatic efforts should make strategic use of international organizations, multilateral institutions and international legal mechanisms to advance national objectives amid complex global developments and threats to regional and international peace and security.
​
Gharibabadi emphasized the need to strengthen legal diplomacy, document violations of the rights of the Iranian people, pursue the legal dimensions of developments and prepare comprehensive legal and political dossiers. He identified efforts to establish the international responsibility of states violating those rights and pursue effective remedies as key priorities.
​
He also called for improving Iran’s participation in international forums, identifying new opportunities within specialized United Nations bodies and expanding targeted consultations with like-minded and independent countries. Building coalitions and securing international support for Iranian initiatives, he added, were essential to effective multilateral diplomacy.
​
The deputy minister underscored coordination among political, legal, media and technical departments, warning against fragmented work and overlapping efforts. He urged officials to encourage innovative proposals, improve the quality of documents and positions, and develop practical, follow-up measures.
​
Gharibabadi also highlighted training young specialists, setting operational priorities and deadlines, and establishing performance indicators. He said officials should be assessed not by activity levels or attendance at international meetings, but by measurable results and their contribution to protecting Iran’s national interests.

🇺🇦 Kiev moves to ban all Russian-language culture nationwide

"Changes to the law are planned. All Russian-language cultural products will fall under the ban," said Olena Ivanovska, Ukraine's commissioner for the protection of the state language, as reported by Times of Ukraine.

The current law, passed in 2022, only bans music created or performed by Russian citizens. Russian-language songs by Ukrainian artists remain legal, something Ivanovska has been trying to change since she took office in July 2025.

Without a national ban, her office has been pressing city councils one by one. Kiev, Dnepropetrovsk, Poltava, Kremenchug, Kropivnitsky and Ternopol have already adopted "moratoriums" banning Russian-language music, films, books and performances in public spaces.

Odessa is the holdout. On October 28, its city council rejected the ban for a second time, with only 18 deputies voting in favor. One deputy called it populist and "a piece of paper nobody will follow."

In early October, Ivanovska urged parliament to fast-track a bill amending the language law. On the same day as the Odessa vote, she also called on Ukraine's National Security and Defense Council to assess the "threats" facing the Ukrainian language.

🖥 Ayatollah Khamenei outlines priorities on economy, national unity, ending war

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei emphasized economic resilience, public welfare, national unity, sustainable security and the protection of Iran’s national interests as key priorities amid the war with the United States and the Israeli regime.

The priorities emerged from separate meetings with President Masoud Pezeshkian, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Judiciary Chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Eje’i and Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Major General Mohsen Rezaei.
​
During a meeting with Pezeshkian in August, the Leader and the president discussed public livelihood needs, the war’s consequences, military developments, employment, housing, foreign economic relations, and the management of domestic currency, foreign exchange and energy resources. Pezeshkian also stressed reforming energy consumption and preventing winter gas and electricity cuts.
​
At a meeting with Ghalibaf in October, the Leader emphasized strengthening national power, preserving social cohesion and unity, and maintaining the public’s informed and deterrent presence in nightly public gatherings. Ghalibaf later told parliament that the Leader was in good health.
​
In his meeting with Mohseni Eje’i, the Leader highlighted expanding justice, protecting public rights and effectively combating corruption as ways to strengthen public trust and social capital.
​
During talks with Rezaei, the Leader described the Supreme National Security Council and its secretariat as a crossroads of national policymaking, emphasizing the interconnectedness of culture, politics, economics, and security.
​
The meetings also addressed military, economic and cognitive warfare, sustainable security, and Iran’s conditions for ending the conflict.
​
During these meetings, the Leader emphasized pursuing the rights and interests of the Iranian people and the Resistance Front by securing the conditions set out by Iranian officials for ending the war and bringing the current state of neither war nor peace to an end.
